timing.note: Apply at 18 and join every list (Arc of Mass).

steps.title: Apply to every open list
steps.detail: The state (EOHLC) list is closed. Apply to local housing authorities' Section 8 lists, MassNAHRO's centralized waiting list, and project-based voucher properties. The state advises applying to both kinds to improve your chances.

steps.title: Wait, and keep your contact info current
steps.detail: If the agency can't reach you when your name comes up, you can lose your place.

steps.title: Get a voucher
steps.detail: When your name comes up and you qualify (for the state program, generally income at or below 50% of Area Median Income), you receive a voucher.

steps.title: Find a home before the voucher expires
steps.detail: You have a limited time to find a rental anywhere in the country. You can also stay in your current home if it meets the program's health and safety standards.

steps.title: Move in and pay your share
steps.detail: You generally pay 30% of income toward rent. The program pays the rest to the landlord, up to a payment standard set by ZIP code.

steps.title: Apply to the developments you want
steps.detail: You can apply to one or all Boston Housing Authority lists you qualify for. Each development has its own list, ranked by bedroom size, priority and preference points, then application date.

steps.title: Wait, and check your status
steps.detail: Call the Status Information Line at (617) 988-3400 or visit the Housing Service Center, 56 Chauncy Street (Mon–Wed, 9am–5pm). You can add or remove developments until BHA schedules your interview.

steps.title: Screening and interview
steps.detail: Near the top of a list, BHA calls to schedule an interview. Bring the Final Application Form, IDs, Social Security cards, citizenship documents, proof of income and assets, and landlord contacts for the last 3 years.

steps.title: Get an offer
steps.detail: Vacancies go to the screened, approved applicant with the oldest application date and highest rank. The bedroom size matches the household.

steps.title: Accept, or decline carefully
steps.detail: Missing final screening or not accepting an offer can withdraw you from all BHA lists. Priority applicants who decline also lose their priority for a year.

timing.note: Use the MassNAHRO Centralized Waiting List instead.

steps.title: Know the state list is closed
steps.detail: EOHLC stopped taking Section 8 mobile voucher applications on Jan 13, 2025, until further notice.

steps.title: Apply for project-based vouchers
steps.detail: Ask your Regional Administering Agency which properties have project-based vouchers, then apply to each property's own waitlist.

steps.title: Apply to local housing authorities
steps.detail: Contact local housing authorities, and apply online to MassNAHRO's centralized Section 8 waiting list.

steps.title: Keep contact info current everywhere
steps.detail: Every list needs to be able to reach you, or you can lose your place.

steps.title: Get emergency help if you need it
steps.detail: RAFT covers short-term housing emergencies. Boston residents at risk of homelessness can ask the City's Continuum of Care about Stability Vouchers.

steps.title: Apply from age 17
steps.detail: Adults with autism can qualify for DDS even without an intellectual disability. DDS encourages applying from age 17, even while still in school.

steps.title: Fill out the Adult Eligibility Application
steps.detail: Applications are by age and in several languages. The Eligibility Fact Sheet for Adult Autism Spectrum Disorders lists the documents needed. Questions: DDS Autism Division, (617) 624-7778, autismdivision@mass.gov.

steps.title: Eligibility decision
steps.detail: DDS reviews the application against its criteria. The Guide to the DDS Eligibility Process explains the criteria and lists regional offices.

steps.title: Meet your Autism Service Coordinator
steps.detail: Once approved, you're matched with a coordinator at your local DDS office, who meets you and your family to learn your needs and goals and explain what DDS offers.

steps.title: Service plan and services
steps.detail: If you use services, the coordinator helps write a Service Plan and checks that it's working. For adults 18+ who have finished high school, services can include job and day supports, help at home, coaching and college navigation, depending on needs and available funding.

steps.title: Contact the school or MassAbility
steps.detail: Students with disabilities ages 14–21 apply through their local MassAbility office or the Pre-ETS provider assigned to their school. Every school has one; the guidance office can say who.

steps.title: Build awareness
steps.detail: First summer jobs, what positions are out there, and help with work permits.

steps.title: Explore careers
steps.detail: Interests, the education and skills a career needs, and possible internships. Services include job exploration, workplace readiness training, work-based learning, counseling on college or training, and self-advocacy and peer mentoring.

steps.title: Hand off to a career counselor
steps.detail: Two years before graduating or turning 22, connect with the provider to start career services. A MassAbility career counselor takes over from the Pre-ETS provider.

timing.note: Reported at capacity as of May 2025.

steps.title: Check fit
steps.detail: Young adults with disabilities, ages 18–30, who want to start or change a career path.

steps.title: Contact a participating MassAbility office
steps.detail: South: Boston, Roxbury, Braintree. North: Lawrence, Lowell. West: Springfield, Worcester. The page doesn't describe how to apply, so ask one of these offices.

steps.title: Get a team
steps.detail: Mentors, counselors, benefits advisors and employment specialists work with each person.

steps.title: Choose a path
steps.detail: A certificate program, on-the-job training, an apprenticeship, or a STEM internship.

timing.note: Inactive for 2+ years means the application closes.

steps.title: Create a CHAMP account
steps.detail: You need an email address, or you can apply on paper in person. No documents are needed to start.

steps.title: Apply and pick housing authorities
steps.detail: Enter contact, housing, household and income details, then choose housing authorities and the type of housing that fits; some units are for people with disabilities. State rental vouchers can be applied for in CHAMP too.

steps.title: Wait on each authority's list
steps.detail: Each housing authority keeps its own waitlist. Veterans and people who live or work in that community have a better chance.

steps.title: Log in every year
steps.detail: Log in to CHAMP or contact a housing agency each year. Applications inactive for 2 years may be closed.

steps.title: Send documents when asked
steps.detail: Near the top of a list, the housing authority asks for documents (such as a birth certificate, pay stubs, bank statements, ID) and a Supplemental Application. Respond even if you don't have everything yet. Some documents expire after 90 days.

steps.title: Accept an offer, or decline carefully
steps.detail: If you turn down 3 offers, you're removed from public housing waitlists at every housing authority.

timing.note: Payment about 14 business days after approval.

steps.title: Check eligibility
steps.detail: You're at risk of losing your housing (for example a Notice to Quit, eviction notice or shutoff notice) and income is under 50% of Area Median Income, or under 60% if at risk of domestic violence. Up to $7,000 per 12 months.

steps.title: Gather documents
steps.detail: ID, proof of current housing such as a lease, proof of the crisis, and income (often verified automatically).

steps.title: Apply, and tell your landlord
steps.detail: Apply online through the Housing Help Hub, or ask your Regional Administering Agency for help. Your landlord must submit their own application within 21 days or yours times out. Some applicants are asked afterward to verify their identity through ID.me; watch for an email with instructions.

steps.title: Review
steps.detail: An agency reviews it and emails you if anything is missing.

steps.title: Payment
steps.detail: After approval, payment goes to the landlord.

kodi_lee_music_grant_max.note: Music lessons, therapy, studio time or equipment. Autistic people 15+; past recipients can't reapply.

autism_alliance_family_grant_max.note: MetroWest families of a child with autism; priority for income up to $60,000 (family of 4).

act_today_grant_max.note: Paid directly to approved providers or vendors. Quarterly cycles; household income considered.
